terms.gloss: of its own accord, by itself
evidence: Liv. 1.39.2: dōnec suā sponte experrēctus esset
terms.comment: Of free will, or of one’s own agency without help: of people, animals and things alike. In good prose always with meā, tuā, suā; the poets also write sponte suā and sponte alone (Lewis & Short).
By itself, without anything else: per sē movētur. Also “in itself” (see the sense of the phrase in each passage).
Without being asked, going further than expected; of a person, rarely of a machine.

phrases.latin: parce, puer, stimulīs et fortius ūtere lōrīs: sponte suā properant; labor est inhibēre volentēs
phrases.english: spare the goad, boy, and use the reins more firmly: they hurry of their own accord; the work is holding them back when they want to go

phrases.latin: movērī vetuisse puerum dōnec suā sponte experrēctus esset
phrases.english: she forbade anyone to move the boy until he woke up by himself
